let r = MagicBento::new(vec![BentoItem::new("Insights", "Analytics", "Track user behavior")]).show(ui);

glowkit-effects::GlassSurface.name: GlassSurface
glowkit-effects::GlassSurface.doc:
A frosted, refracting glass panel over any backdrop.

egui can't read back what is already on screen, so the backdrop is supplied as a painter
closure. The panel paints it normally, then paints a second copy inside the glass that is
bent toward the rim (content just outside the edge is pulled in and compressed, like light
through a thick pane), optionally magnified, blurred and split into red/blue fringes, then
tinted and lit with specular edge highlights. Your content goes on top of the glass.

Turn on [`GlassSurface::lens`] and [`GlassSurface::follow_pointer`] for a liquid lens that
glides after the pointer.

glowkit-interactions::SplitShowcase.name: SplitShowcase
glowkit-interactions::SplitShowcase.doc:

At rest the halves read as a single rounded capsule split by a dotted line. Hover a half and
it springs outward, peeling away from its partner: the corners along the seam round out,
the card brightens and lifts, while the other half gives way slightly. Pressing squishes the
card. Motion is a soft, Apple-style spring.

glowkit-interactions::HoverImageList.name: HoverImageList
glowkit-interactions::HoverImageList.doc:

glowkit-interactions::SwipeActions.name: SwipeActions
glowkit-interactions::SwipeActions.doc:
A message list whose rows slide sideways to reveal actions, like a mail app.

it springs shut. Dragging further than the buttons meets growing rubber-band resistance,
except on the delete side: past 60% of the row the Delete button stretches across the whole
row with a little lurch, and releasing there collapses the row away. Only one row stays open
at a time; tapping a row closes it.

glowkit-interactions::ArcPicker.name: ArcPicker

glowkit-interactions::WheelPicker.name: WheelPicker

glowkit-interactions::SortableStack.name: SortableStack
glowkit-interactions::SortableStack.doc:

bigger, with a deeper shadow) while the other cards glide out of its way on springs; drop it
and it settles into its new slot. The numbers re-count themselves, the circle ticks a task off,
and "Undo reorder" puts the last order back.

glowkit-interactions::CardDealer.name: CardDealer
glowkit-interactions::CardDealer.doc:
A card table: a deck in the corner deals cards that arc into a fanned hand, flipping face up
in flight. Sort and shuffle send every card gliding to its new place in the fan, and collect
sweeps them all back onto the deck. Every card rides its own position, rotation and flip
springs, so actions can overlap mid-flight.

setters.doc: Most cards the hand holds.

glowkit-interactions::BloomMenu.name: BloomMenu
glowkit-interactions::BloomMenu.doc:

the panel (width, height, position and corner radius all morph), its label glides up into
the panel's title, the plus turns into the close cross, and the tiles pop in one after
another. Closing plays the same morph backwards.

[`BloomMenu::show`] returns the index of the tile picked this frame.

glowkit-interactions::ExpandableActionBa.name: ExpandableActionBar
glowkit-interactions::ExpandableActionBa.doc:
A floating toolbar of icons that unfolds into labelled actions. Each slot widens on its own
slightly staggered spring, so the bar ripples open from left to right: labels and keyboard
hints slide out from behind the icons, notification badges ride along, and a soft highlight
glides between whichever action is under the pointer. A pill below toggles it.

tiles near the middle swell and bow outward, tiles at the rim shrink and fall into a
vignette. Drag to pan and fling to coast; the lens bends every tile (each is a subdivided,
textured mesh) as it slides past.

glowkit-motion::LayoutAnim.doc:
Animates items between layout positions and sizes, keyed by identity (FLIP-style).

Each item reserves its *target* space in the layout, but is drawn in its *animated* rect, on
a layer above its siblings while moving. Content is laid out inside the animated rect (so a
growing card really grows, text re-wraps, buttons stay clickable where they are drawn).
Positions are tracked relative to the container's origin, so scrolling never triggers
animations.

Reusing a key in a different place (e.g. a thumbnail in a grid, then a large detail view)
makes the item fly from one place to the other, a shared element ("layout id") transition.

glowkit-motion::Draggable.name: Draggable
glowkit-motion::Draggable.doc:
Makes its contents draggable, with momentum and physics.

* `axis`: lock to X or Y.
* `constraints`: a rect (in the same coordinates as the `Ui`) the content must stay inside;
  dragging past it rubber-bands by `elastic`.
* `momentum`: on release the content keeps gliding with the pointer's velocity and bounces
  back inside the constraints.
* `snap_points` / `snap_to_origin`: on release, spring to the snap point nearest to where
  momentum would have taken it.
* `while_drag` / `while_hover`: props layered on top during those gestures.

Buttons inside keep working: only drags that start on empty space move the content.

glowkit-interactions::OtpAutofill.name: OtpAutofill

code that just arrived. Tap the suggestion and the digits type themselves in one by one, each
popping into its slot. Once every slot is filled the code is checked against

row with a damped spring, flashes it red and clears it. The keypad and the keyboard both type
too (backspace deletes).

glowkit-interactions::PourFilter.name: PourFilter
glowkit-interactions::PourFilter.doc:
A filter bar of liquid ink. Tap a tag and the result-count pill pours into it: a tongue of
ink runs across, floods the chip and swallows it into the pill while the count rolls down.
Tap it again and the ink drains back, necks and snaps free. The ink is a real implicit
surface (smooth-unioned rounded rects, marched into a mesh), so merges and splits are fluid.

`selected` is caller-owned (one flag per tag). The response reports `changed()` on toggles.
glowkit-interactions::PourFilter.example:
use glowkit::interactions::PourFilter;
ui.add(PourFilter::new(&["Sauna", "Lakeside", "Dogs OK", "Hot tub"], &mut on).total(86).noun("cabins"));

sticks to the top until the next one pushes it away.

your finger and either completes the pop or springs back, depending on distance and speed.
Press and hold the back link to open a history menu of all ancestors and jump straight to

glowkit-interactions::CoachTip.name: CoachTip
glowkit-interactions::CoachTip.doc:
A TipKit-style feature tip that points at a control (or sits inline in a list).

As a popover it grows out of its arrow on a bouncy spring, anchored under the control you
point it at. It is tactile: drag it and it follows with rubber-band resistance, fling it and it
flies off in that direction and is dismissed; let go gently and it springs home. The close
button shrinks it back into its arrow. As an inline card ([`CoachTip::inline`]) it unfolds
into the layout, pushing content down, and folds away when closed. Dismissal is remembered
per id ([`CoachTip::dismissed`], [`CoachTip::reset`]), so several tips can be shown one after
another.

within the timeout and the row unfolds back into place with a soft highlight; let the ring
run out, swipe the bar down, or delete something else, and the deletion is committed (removed
from your `Vec`). The countdown pauses while the pointer rests on the bar. A second delete
while the bar is up commits the first and the bar gives a little bump as its text changes.

glowkit-interactions::ConfirmSheet.doc:
A confirmation prompt that rises as an action sheet on phones and pops as an alert on wide
screens.

Press the trigger and the screen dims while the sheet springs up from the bottom: the title,
description and destructive action share one rounded group, with **Cancel** on its own card
below. The sheet is physical: drag it down and it follows (let go past a threshold, or flick,
to dismiss), push it up and it resists like rubber. On wide areas it shows as an alert that
scales in from slightly large. Buttons squish when pressed.

glowkit-interactions::ActiveSessions.name: ActiveSessions
glowkit-interactions::ActiveSessions.doc:

The current device is pinned at the top and cannot be signed out. Every other row has a
**Sign out** button: press it and a small spinner spins for a moment (like a real request),

glowkit-ai::Markdown.name: Markdown
glowkit-ai::Markdown.doc:
Renders Markdown the way AI chat products do: comfortable line height, highlighted code blocks
with a copy button, clean tables, lists, quotes and links.

It is built for streaming: pass the text received so far every frame and half-written syntax
(an open ```` ``` ```` fence, a dangling `**`) never flashes on screen. Optionally the newest
characters fade in ([`Markdown::fade_tail`]) and a blinking caret follows the text.

frame, tolerates half-written tags, and fades new elements in as they arrive.

(`variant="outline|secondary|ghost|destructive"`), `Badge` (`variant`), `Row` / `HStack`,
`Stack` / `VStack` / `Col`, `Input` (`placeholder`), `Separator`, `Progress` (`value` 0-100),
`Avatar` (`name`), `Switch` (`checked`), `Image` (`ratio`), `Stat` (`label`, `value`, `delta`),

glowkit-agents::CopilotSidebar.doc:

glowkit-canvas::NodeEditor.name: NodeEditor
glowkit-canvas::NodeEditor.doc:
A node-graph editor (React Flow / xyflow pattern).

* Drag nodes (multi-selection drags together, snap-to-grid), shift-click to add to the
  selection, shift-drag on the background for a selection box.
* Drag from a handle to connect, with a live preview, magnetic snapping and highlighted valid
  targets; drag a connected input to detach / reconnect.
* Bezier / smooth-step / step / straight edges, animated edges, labels.
* Minimap, controls (zoom, fit, lock, layout, snap), node toolbar, undo/redo,
  copy/paste/duplicate, delete, layered auto-layout, `?` shortcut sheet.

glowkit-templates::AppShell.name: AppShell
glowkit-templates::AppShell.doc:

card, user card), topbar (sidebar toggle, breadcrumb, Ctrl+K search that opens a command
palette, notifications bell with a dropdown, theme toggle, user menu) and your content.

The navigation tree ([`NavSection`] / [`NavItem`](super::NavItem)) and the active route are
owned by you. The sidebar collapses to an icon rail on a spring (Ctrl+B or the toggle), auto
collapses when the window gets narrow, and turns into a drawer on phone widths. Toasts,
dialogs and the palette are kept inside the shell.

sparks from the cut. Healing pours in with a green ghost, a bright sweep and rising pluses.
Low health pulses red.

pops in on a spring with a big PAUSED heading, optional info rows (chapter, play time) and
the menu entries staggering in; closing reverses it. Draw it over your game view.

glowkit-interactions::GameSettingsPanel.name: GameSettingsPanel
glowkit-interactions::GameSettingsPanel.doc:
A tabbed game settings panel: Graphics, Audio and Controls. The active tab's underline glides
on a spring and content slides in from the side you moved toward. Rows include segmented
sliders (drag or scroll), springy toggles, ◀ value ▶ selectors and key rebind rows: click a
key cap, it pulses "press a key", and the next key press is captured (Esc cancels; duplicate
bindings turn red).

glowkit-interactions::GameAchievementToa.doc:

a light sweep across the card, then a thin timer line runs down before it slides away. Feed
it the seconds since the achievement unlocked; outside its lifetime it paints nothing (but
keeps its space so layouts don't jump).
glowkit-interactions::GameAchievementToa.example:
use glowkit::interactions::{GameAchievementToast, GameIcon};
ui.add(GameAchievementToast::new("Dragonslayer", "Defeat Vorrhak on Hard", GameIcon::Trophy).points(50).age(1.2));
